metric_and_harness.definition_H1: VERIFIED (orchestrator read src/srsvd_jax/steady.py at 66e15d4 himself). STEADY5_GB = store bytes of blocks whose device result was confirmed ready between window_open and window_close, normalised to exactly 300 s (bytes x 300 / span). window_open = first block confirmation after warm-up AND >= 32 blocks streamed; window_close = first block confirmation at or after window_open + 300.0 s; both instants are a block_until_ready on every outstanding block; span must lie in [300.0, 302.0]. If the job completes inside the window the next identical job starts IMMEDIATELY in the same process (same reader, same pool, no re-pin, same compiled executables); the process runs until the window has closed AND >= 1 full job has completed with its gate printed. compiles_in_window must be 0. FROZEN at H1.
metric_and_harness.record_eligibility: INHERITED from the contract. fixed store on /lscratch; ONE L40S by UUID with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES printed, ECC clean; mode direct; k=32 p=10 q=2 seed 0 (3 passes); gate PASS (G1 1e-4, G2 1e-3, G3 1e-2, G4 5e-2 two-sided) on >= 1 complete job in-process; compiles_in_window == 0; unprofiled; both installed SHAs printed from inside the job and equal to the claimed commits; harness H1; same-iteration champion control; margin > noise floor and >= 1 pct. Numerics-affecting (wire dtype, matmul precision, accumulation dtype) eligible if the gate passes, labelled. Never eligible: fewer passes / changed q,k,p; any dtype ON DISK; buffered / page cache; > 1 card; another tier; profiled.

metric_and_harness.harness_design_decisions_H1: VERIFIED by source read. (D1) every block carries a process-global monotone seq and its byte count; SteadyWindow keeps a pending deque and folds it on confirm, so counting is exact to the block and the open/close drains cannot double count. (D2) the warm-up runs on JOB 1 ONLY; jobs 2+ reuse a warm session and skip it, because the warm-up exists only to move COMPILATION out of the measured region. (D2b, found by the implementer and not in the brief) core.make_step returns a NEW closure per call and jax keys its caches on the function object, so the jitted step is SESSION STATE -- without hoisting it, job 2 would recompile inside the window. (D3) the hot path adds one integer increment and one deque append per block; the only added host syncs in the whole process are the two _drain calls at open and close, charged to sync site 'steady:window'. (D4) with steady=None every line is whole-job HEAD's behaviour.

hardware.HOST_READ_REGRESSION_iteration_4: RESOLVED IN ITERATION 7, AND IT WAS NOT A HARDWARE REGRESSION. The phenomenon: between two byte-identical champion runs 47 minutes apart the in-pipeline /lscratch read fell 33.773 -> 24.402 GB/s as a STEP and never recovered. SEVEN CAUSES REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT: NVMe thermal/device state (12 min proven idle changed nothing; raw dd 12 pct FASTER than iteration 1); the reader or pool machinery (the same library's standalone probe reads 36.88 in the same hour); other tenants (constant load, zero writes, all six members within 0.04 pct); huge pages (cliff sweep flat across a 16x pool-size change, and the pools were never THP-eligible); pool size; cudaHostRegister pinning; a live CUDA context (the last three tie to within 0.60 pct, inside the noise floor). THE CAUSE: the in-thread f32->bf16 cast. Iteration 7's c7a-wire-f32 -- the champion pipeline with the cast switched off, same GPU consumer, same PCIe DMA, same pools -- reads 35.410523 GB/s against the control mean 24.305784, +45.6876 pct, closing the probe-versus-pipeline gap from 12.5 GB/s to 1.4. The cast's cost rose from +4.24 pct of the read in iteration 3 to +45.7 pct, because it runs inside the reader worker threads on a node whose usable CPU is contended by seven root wekanode processes pegged at 100 pct. THE FIX: --convert-threads 4, which restores the read to 34.239527 GB/s and took the record to 9909.201421 GB.
hardware.node_is_not_exclusive_in_practice: VERIFIED (iteration 5). Despite --exclusive and OverSubscribe=NO, eleven root-owned wekanode processes run continuously, seven of them pegged at 100-101 pct CPU and hard-pinned to single cpus (pids 8645->cpu32, 8646->cpu33, others psr 29/30/31/34/35), plus four more at 29.0/24.8/16.0/11.1 pct. loadavg 12.24/14.41/18.47 with our job idle. squeue -w sdfada015 shows only our job. nproc 58 vs SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE 72. This is a constant background, not a confound between rows, but it is why host-side CPU headroom is smaller than the cpuset suggests.
hardware.NUMA_REGIME: VERIFIED (iterations 8-9), THE CAMPAIGN'S DOMINANT NON-DETERMINISM. A per-process fast/slow read regime (~30-35 vs ~24.3-24.5 GB/s) is chosen at process start and held for the process's life; every job within a run agrees and mode membership does not track the configuration. CAUSE: NUMA page placement. Free memory at an iteration-9 launch was 25089 / 2878 / 4415 / 6274 MB on nodes 0/1/2/3 of ~193 GB each, so default local allocation puts the 5368750080 B staging pool on whichever node the touching thread is on and three of four are starved. numactl --interleave=all reaches the fast regime on demand: 9874.654290 GB, read 34.225764 GB/s, +38.016 pct over a three-control bracket that agreed to 0.2064 pct, with the pool residency flag OFF so the gain is placement not residency. n=1 as of iteration 9; iteration 10 replicates. THIS IS WHY every iteration from 9 onward carries THREE controls and spreads candidate repeats across the iteration. ITERATION 10 CORRECTION: interleave does NOT CAUSE the fast regime -- a default-placement control reached 9764.407 -- it HOLDS it. Interleave is fast 8/8 across iterations 9-11; default about 3/13; membind=0 0/1. The mechanism is SPREADING, not starvation-avoidance: node 0 is the only node with real free memory (25 GB vs 2.9/5.2/7.8) and binding the pool there is the SLOWEST configuration measured, at -27.37 pct, with 24 CPUs available inside the cpuset so it was not CPU-starved. One memory controller cannot feed 16 reader threads plus the PCIe DMA.
